key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of metal halide perovskites from early-time spectra, generalizing across compositions and crystallinities.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more scalable stability screening for perovskite solar-cell materials, reducing the need for lengthy accelerated-aging experiments.
method: Collected 167 perovskite samples under heat and illumination stress
Featurized >86k photoluminescence spectra with a physics-informed model
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen samples
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model outperforms baseline benchmarks and generalizes across material groups using a dataset of 167 materials and over 86k PL spectra.
watch_item: Performance may depend on high-quality, consistently measured PL time-series data, so transfer to different instruments or stress protocols may require recalibration.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
